WOODLAND · permissive-occupancy step, rejected by the family
4 Jul 1955 · Possession order enforced
4 Jul 1955 · High Court possession order enforced: “possession was taken in respect of all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden”
RECORD · judgment recital · grade 2
The Court of Appeal records that WGR obtained a High Court possession order against Frederick Buckler “in respect of the whole of the farm”, and: “On July 4 1955 that possession order was enforced, and possession was taken in respect of all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden.” It gives the reason: Mary “had recently come out of hospital after having had a leg amputated and was objecting very strongly to leaving the farmhouse.” Working hypothesis (not a record; the order, warrant, execution return and plan are not yet assembled): the order was made against Frederick, whose farm tenancy had ended, and the land WGR let is the eastern fields, Parcel B, on the 1939 WGR plan (EV-0023). On the 1947 Ordnance Survey (25-inch, Glamorgan sheet XLVII.6, revised 1941) the Ty-mawr house and yard sit between the wooded old limekiln and quarry ground to the north and the open ground to the south-east. The Three Parts of Parcel A page identifies those two areas as Parcel A’s woodland and green, with the farmhouse and garden as the third part. Taking “all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden” therefore took the woodland and the green along with Parcel B, and left Mary in the third part, the house. This station sits on Parcel B; the woodland and the green have their own lines. The order and execution return (EV-0032, EV-0034) are not published here.
Source: 1987 judgment · The 1955 Possession Order · EV-0023 · 1947 Ordnance Survey (sheet XLVII.6) · Three Parts of Parcel A · EV-0032 · EV-0034
7 May 1958 · Leckwith Common inquiry
7 May 1958 · Cardiff City Council’s Leckwith Common inquiry (Leckwith Common, not Great House Farm or Parcel A)
VERIFIED · press (OCR)
Mary appears in the press under her married name, Mrs Buckler. At the 6 May 1958 inquiry into Cardiff City Council’s plan to turn Leckwith Common into playing fields, the Western Mail (7 May 1958, p.7) reports: “Mrs. Mary Doreen Buckler, of Great House Farm, Llandough, said she did not oppose the proposal so long as it applied only to playing fields. About 130 years ago Lord Bute allowed her family ‘a slice of land’ which was now Leckwith Common.” The inquiry concerned Leckwith Common, not Great House Farm or Parcel A. Quoted from the newspaper archive’s OCR; page image not seen.
Source: EV-0035
20 Nov 1958 · Mary’s public objection
19–20 Nov 1958 · Mary objects to Glamorgan County Council’s planning committee: her land “walked in and taken”
VERIFIED · press (OCR)
The Western Mail (20 November 1958, p.7) reports the planning committee meeting of 19 November 1958: “Mrs. M D. Buckler was objecting to further industrial development in the vicinity of her farm, Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough.” Land farmed by her family since 1667 had been “wrongfully appropriated”. “This is a Welsh case of Crichel Down,” said Mrs. Buckler. “The Glamorgan County Council, Penarth Urban and Cardiff Rural Councils and Western Ground Rents have walked in and taken …” “Mrs. Buckler claimed that the water was cut off from her house and grounds for nearly 10 years by order of Western Ground Rents.” Quoted from the newspaper archive’s OCR (search-result snippets; the sentence breaks off after “taken”); page image not seen.
Source: EV-0037
1958/9 · Tenancy offer refused
1958/9 · WGR offers Mary (Nancy) Williams a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden; she refuses it, and later alternative accommodation
RECORD · judgment recital · grade 2
The Court of Appeal records that by 1959 Mary asserted title to Great House Farm through her grandfather, John Williams, and: “She was offered a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden by Western Ground Rents but refused to accept it. She was also later offered, and refused, alternative accommodation.” The green lies south of the house and garden, now the Church View Close park, and was registered as village green VG41 on 16 June 1970. The offer and her reply (EV-0039) are not published here.
Source: 1987 judgment · EV-0039 · EV-0044

29 Mar 1961 · Woodland deed
29 Mar 1961 · Deed between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City Corporation, recited on the woodland register
RECORD · register recital · grade 2 (deed not read)
The woodland register WA735527 lists “a Deed dated 29 March 1961 made between (1) Western Ground Rents Limited (2) The South Western Brick & Tile Company Limited and (3) Cardiff City Corporation”; the land tinted pink is subject to the rights in it, and the register notes “Copy filed under WA231076”. The deed and its plan (EV-0040) have not been inspected, so its terms and precise extent, and what Cardiff City Corporation received, are not known. The 1994 transfer to Forest of Cardiff, from Ideal Homes Wales Ltd (register WA735527, entry 8), is a separate record; no transfer from Cardiff City Corporation is on record.
Source: EV-0040 · EV-0169 · register WA735527

11 Dec 1962 · Possession order
11 Dec 1962 · Possession order: farmhouse and garden. The BP house line starts here
VERIFIED · judgment
The Court of Appeal records that WGR sued Frederick and Mary Buckler in Cardiff County Court “for possession of the farmhouse and garden and mesne profits since 1955”, that “On December 11 1962 a possession order was made by Judge Temple Morris QC”, and that “nothing was done before 1974 to enforce the 1962 possession order”. The original order and plan (EV-0041) are not published here.
Source: 1987 judgment · EV-0041 · The 1962 Possession Order
1965 · Weekly tenancy offer
1965 · Further weekly tenancy offer; not signed, no rent paid
VERIFIED · judgment
Recorded in the Court of Appeal’s history: in March 1965 WGR’s agents offered Mrs Buckler a tenancy. Not signed; no rent paid.
Source: 1987 judgment · EV-0039
1967 · Lands Tribunal v Cardiff
1967 · Lands Tribunal: WGR v City of Cardiff
VERIFIED · catalogue only
A compulsory-purchase compensation case, catalogued at The National Archives. Which land it concerned has not been read.
Source: TNA catalogue entry
31 Dec 1969 · BP acquires
31 Dec 1969 · WGR → BP Pension Trust: BP takes WGR’s interest, including the 1962 order
VERIFIED · judgment
Conveyance recited as the root of BP’s title. The instrument and plan (EV-0043) are not published here. The same conveyance carried Parcel B, so the station shows on both lines. In September 1974 BP applied for leave to enforce the 1962 order, so it held that order’s benefit.
Source: 1987 judgment · EV-0043
GREEN · usual 12-year waiting period · measured: about 11–12 yrs (1958/9 → 16 Jun 1970)
16 Jun 1970 · Village green VG41
16 Jun 1970 · Village green VG41 registered by Glamorgan County Council
REPORTED · grade 3 · application, map and ownership section not yet read
The date as recorded on the wiki. The application, map and ownership section of the VG41 file are not published here; registration as a green does not by itself show who owns it. Llandough Community Council states that it “owns and maintains the village green”.
Source: EV-0044 · community council website

1971 · Ordnance Survey altered
1971 · Ordnance Survey sheet prints “Ty Mawr Farm” in a new position
RECORD · map and name book · grade 1; reason: open question
On the Ordnance Survey 1:2500 sheet revised 1969 (published 1971) the name appears as “Ty Mawr Farm”, placed west of where earlier editions printed “Ty-mawr” (OS object name book, EV-0252). Why the name moved is an open question. On the earlier OS editions of 25-inch sheet XLVII.6 (1900, 1920 and 1947) the “Ty-mawr” name sits on the house parcel, Parcel A. The one 1971 record known on this line is BP Pension Trust’s 1971 abstract of title, known only from later recitals (EV-0045).
Source: EV-0045 · OS sheet XLVII.6, 1947
1974 · BP action unheard; letters follow
1974 · BP Pension Trust’s county-court possession action adjourned part heard and never listed again; leave to enforce the 1962 order obtained, warrant later withdrawn; the licence letters follow (31 Oct)
RECORD · press (grade 4) + judgment recital (grade 2)
On 15 April 1974 Mary opened the farmhouse to the public and said: “my solicitors tell me I have a valid claim to it” (Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974). BP brought a fresh county-court action for possession; on 3 July 1974 the hearing was adjourned part heard for a formal defence; Mary’s defence then pleaded that she owned the house parcel, relying on the Limitation Act 1939. It was never listed again. BP also obtained leave on 19 Sep 1974 to enforce the 1962 order; Mary’s solicitors appealed because she had not been given notice, and after BP’s licence letters of 31 Oct 1974 the landlords’ solicitors withdrew the warrant, at a date before 25 Nov 1974. The court papers are not published here (EV-0049).
Source: EV-0048 · EV-0049 · The 1974 Licence Letters
31 Oct 1974 · BP licence letters
31 Oct 1974 · BP letters offer continued rent-free occupancy of the house
VERIFIED · judgment
The letters were one-sided: the judgment records that Mrs Buckler “never expressly accepted or rejected the terms of the two letters”. In July 1974 her defence had asserted that the claim was barred by adverse possession. The Court of Appeal (1987) held: “whether she liked it or not, from the time of her receipt of the letters, Mrs Buckler was in possession of the farmhouse and garden by the licence of BP Properties Ltd, and her possession was no longer adverse” (Dillon LJ).
Source: EV-0050 · EV-0080

23 Feb 1983 · BP applies: house
23 Feb 1983 · BP Properties Ltd applies to register WA240304 (farmhouse and garden)
RECORD · HMLR schedule · grade 3
HMLR’s schedule dates the Form 1C and first register edition 23 Feb 1983; examination continued to May 1983. Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 Mar 1983.
Source: EV-0066 · EV-0063
BP HOUSE · registration (source pending) · we say · source pending
2 Feb 1987 · WA240304 amalgamated
2 Feb 1987 · WA240304 amalgamated into WA231076 while the appeal is pending
RECORD · HMLR schedule · grade 3
Amalgamation recorded during the appeal. Whether it changed extent, class of title, parties’ rights or the issues on appeal awaits the application, plan and registrar’s notes; the application and plan (EV-0078) are not published here.
Source: EV-0078 · 1987 amalgamation
31 Jul 1987 · Court of Appeal
31 Jul 1987 · Court of Appeal: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2
VERIFIED · judgment
The appeal concerned the farmhouse and garden only. The Court of Appeal (1987) held: “whether she liked it or not, from the time of her receipt of the letters, Mrs Buckler was in possession of the farmhouse and garden by the licence of BP Properties Ltd, and her possession was no longer adverse”, so the adverse-possession claim to the farmhouse and garden failed. From here no register shows the Williams Parcel A title; the line runs on unregistered.
Source: judgment (BAILII) · EV-0080
